questions.question: Explain why people long ago paid such close attention to the Moon.
questions.expected_answer: Before electric lights, the Moon was the brightest light at night, so people could travel and work by its light. Its phases repeat about every twenty-nine and a half days, so people used it as a calendar to count months and to plan planting, harvesting and gatherings.

questions.question: Retell the San and Khoikhoi story of the Moon and the hare in your own words.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon wanted to tell people that, just as it dies and comes back every month, they would also die and come back. It sent the hare with the message, but the hare got it wrong and told people they would die and never come back. The Moon was angry and struck the hare across the mouth, which is why the hare has a split lip.

questions.question: Explain how cultural stories about the Moon are different from science, and why both are valuable.
questions.expected_answer: Science explains the Moon using careful observations and tests, for example that its phases come from seeing different amounts of its sunlit half. Cultural stories explain the Moon in ways that teach lessons, bring families together and keep cultures alive. Both are valuable, and we can learn from and respect both.
